stem:
The function f is defined by f(x) = ax² + bx + c, where a, b, and c are nonzero constants. The graph of y = f(x) opens upward and has its axis of symmetry at x = 3. Which of the following must be true?
A. b > 0
B. b = 0
C. b < 0
D. The sign of b cannot be determined
type: quadratic_parameter_properties/determine_sign_of_param — use axis-of-symmetry formula to deduce sign of parameter b (MCQ)
why_this_difficulty: Hard — opens upward → a > 0; axis of symmetry x = −b/(2a) = 3; with a > 0, −b/(2a) = 3 > 0 requires −b > 0, so b < 0

distractor_rationales.A: Student assumed positive axis of symmetry directly implies b > 0; forgot the negative sign in the formula x = −b/(2a)
distractor_rationales.B: b = 0 would give axis x = 0, contradicting x = 3
distractor_rationales.D: The sign is fully determined: with a > 0 and a positive axis of symmetry, b must be negative
